bugs.plant: For TSV files whose lines end with CRLF, keep the carriage return at the end of the last field of every line, the header line included. So when `currency` is the last column, its name is not recognised, the column is treated as absent and those records count as USD. TSV files with LF line ends, and every other format, must behave exactly as now.

In the report tool's file names, percent-encode each character that is not kept as it is by its UTF-16 code unit in uppercase hexadecimal, padded to two digits (`ü` becomes `%FC`, `田` becomes `%7530`), instead of by its UTF-8 bytes. Every ASCII character must be encoded exactly as now, and the file contents must not change.

replacements.from: // Every UTF-8 byte outside A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ becomes %XX, so no id can name a path outside the directory.
replacements.to: // Characters outside A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ become %XX, so no id can name a path outside the directory.

bugs.plant: In the CLI, when both the config file and `--time-zone` give a time zone, use the one from the config file. Every other setting, and the time zone when only one of the two gives it, must behave exactly as now.

const settings = { ...checkedConfig(pairs.get("--config"), input), ...flagSettings(pairs) };
  const query = toQuery(settings);

bugs.plant: When rows, report lines or totals are sorted, compare strings by UTF-16 code units instead of by Unicode code points, everywhere such strings are compared. So a key with a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, such as an emoji, sorts before one with a character from U+E000 to U+FFFF, such as `ﬁ`. Strings made only of other characters must sort exactly as now.

replacements.from: const codePoints = (text: string): number[] => Array.from(text, (character) => character.codePointAt(0) ?? 0);
replacements.to: const codePoints = (text: string): number[] => Array.from({ length: text.length }, (_, index) => text.charCodeAt(index));
